newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Baht reference rate on the firm side - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Baht reference rate on the firm side - analysts.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand (BoT)'s reference rate for the Thai baht of 27.383 set on Thursday was on the firm side -- in terms of the baht -- considering the price action on Wednesday, analysts said.
"It's on the firm side of the trading range," said Andrew Dermot Fung, regional treasury economist at Standard Chartered in Singapore.
The onshore rate was quoted at 28.000/29.000 with the offshore rate at 0643 GMT at 28.900/400.
Dealers reported quiet trading conditions and said volume continued light.
They noted that on Wednesday the dramatic plunge in the value of the offshore baht saw some stale bears bail out of their remaining short baht forwards.
"A lot of remaining shorts were cleared out yesterday, I think people were relieved to cover," said one trader, adding that he saw no fresh short positions.

"While you can say the BOT collected the rates yesterday and it was a purely mechanical calculation, I would have thought there was some freedom for them to have set the rate higher if they had wanted to."
The rate is six pecent away from the 25.85 the dollar/baht onshore rate was trading at before the news of the managed float was sprung on the market.
The offshore rate hit a quoted peak of 29.25 on Wednesday, a near 20 percent rise from before the announcement.

Given that price action some in the market had thought the BoT might decide to bite harder on the devaluation bullet and today's reference rate would be nearer 10 percent away from the post announcement onshore rate.
"I thought they may put it closer to 28.00 but they are erring on the more conservative side," said Chiang Yao Chye, economist at CIBC Wood Gundy in Singapore.
Analysts said Thursday's firm-looking rate and the two point rise in interest rates clearly shows the Thais do not want the baht to go too far too quickly.
With capital controls still in place the offshore market will remain illiquid and a dangerous place to be short, but over time the offshore and onshore rates will tend to converge, analysts said.
But the onshore rate will tend to converge on the offshore so has further to fall, and convergence looks likely to take place in the upper 20s for dollar/baht, analysts said.
"Assuming interest rates are allowed to come down and there is some recovery in the export sector, I think the baht will move to trade around the 29.00 region," CIBC's Chiang said.
